name: Reuel
overview: The name Reuel appears in Scripture referring to several individuals, notably a son of Esau through his wife Bashemath, whose descendants became chiefs in Edom, as detailed in Genesis 36. Reuel is also identified as the father-in-law of Moses, who is called Jethro or Jether, highlighting his role in the Exodus narrative (Exodus 2). Additionally, the name appears as Deuel, the father of Eliasaph from the tribe of Gad (Numbers 1), and as a Benjamite, showing the diversity of persons bearing this name across different tribes and contexts.
